title: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs
description: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are capable low-level controllers, but they tie where objects go to the layouts they were trained on: when objects are moved or obstacles block the way, they carry them to the wrong place or into collisions. Fine-tuning on new layouts needs robot data for each one and erodes skills the model already has. We introduce Cairn, which keeps the VLA frozen and steers it at test time along learned 3D trajectories of the object in its gripper. The prior and the VLA form the two levels of a hierarchical planner in which feedback runs both ways: the VLA's intended motion chooses and reshapes the trajectories, and the chosen one guides the VLA's denoising. Its predicted actions, mapped to the held object's poses through the grasp, are pulled toward the next waypoint, while the VLA's weights stay untouched. title: ProbFaS: Probabilistic Video Frame Selection for MLLMs via Multi-Fidelity Calibration
description: Processing long videos with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is prohibitively expensive, making informative frame selection essential for accurate video understanding. The default uniform sampling often misses task-relevant keyframes, while recent training-free selectors instead pick frames by how well each one matches the question under an image-text alignment (ITA) score. However, we show that ITA signals correspond poorly with the MLLM's true needs: their rankings correlate weakly with downstream accuracy and are even negatively correlated on over 40% of questions, whereas the MLLM's internal yes/no judgment yields a much stronger signal. We present ProbFaS, a training- and label-free probabilistic pipeline that fuses both signals for key frame selection. ProbFaS treats dense ITA scores as cheap, biased measurements and sparse MLLM judgments as accurate, costly ones, unifying them via co-kriging, a multi-fidelity Gaussian process, to calibrate relevance across all frames. A temporal determinantal point process then selects frames capturing relevance peaks while preserving temporal coverage. title: Guidance as Variance Matching
description: Guidance repels the prediction of a diffusion model away from a weaker reference prediction. It substantially improves sample quality, but its mechanism remains poorly understood. We first find that, at the scales used in practice, guidance does not improve the prediction of the posterior mean (the model's training target); it makes the prediction worse, while samples improve. Second, posterior-mean predictions have less variance than the data, and we find that guidance restores it. We introduce variance-matched guidance: a closed-form rule that picks the guidance scale by matching the variance of the guided predictions to that of the data. Without tuning, it recovers the hand-picked scales of eleven widely used models across image, video, audio, motion, and world generation; to our knowledge, no previous explanation of guidance predicts them. Applied per noise level, it yields a schedule without tuned hyperparameters that users prefer to hand-crafted ones on SD 3.5 Medium. Third, we offer an interpretation of the mechanism behind guidance: each model makes a random error in predicting the posterior mean, and guidance rescales the difference of these errors into a sample with the posterior's covariance, which improves sampling. This view also suggests two new hypotheses that our experiments support: guidance can work with negative scales, and guiding a model with its own checkpoint needs a larger scale than guiding it with an independently trained model.
author: Ali Backour, Artem Lukoianov, Frank Permenter, Tommi Jaakkola, Justin Solomon

General note on MOSS-Image: Through the personal testing I've done and what I've seen from others: MOSS is not the ideal candidate for anime style LORAs as of right now, especially compared to a model like Anima. Anima (v1.1): 0.8 – 1.2 (1.0 sweet spot; Euler / Euler a / er_sde, 25–30 steps, CFG 4.0–5.0; trained on Anima Base and tested on WAI-ANIMA;

description:
NegBeta Dual3 IL - Toward WAI, Away from NoobAI (Illustrious) adds WAI finish and removes NoobAI paint, the cleanest line-quality variant in the batch.

[Recipe] Two stacked differences on UNet only: Nova Anime XL IL v19.0 + 0.25 x (WAI-illustrious IL v1.0 - Nova Anime XL IL v19.0) + -0.12 x (NoobAI-XL EPS Four-Mix (CyberFix) - Nova Anime XL IL v19.0). VAE and text encoders inherited from Nova Anime XL IL v19.0.

[Why this direction] NegBeta uses a negative beta: the second difference is subtracted instead of added.
